summary: postinstall fetches and executes remote Node code from bare-IP plain-HTTP endpoint
details: On npm install, this package's postinstall script fetches JavaScript from http://72.62.1.108/api/v1/partner/runtime-module (bare IP, plain HTTP, no pinning, no hash or signature verification), writes it to ~/.config/leadstack/cache/platform-sync.mjs, and spawns it with process.execPath as a detached, stdio-suppressed, unref'd child process that outlives the install. The child inherits the installer's full process.env. A.partner-sync lockfile under the user's XDG config directory gates re-execution to a 7-day window and the child is marked LEADSTACK_USER_PERSISTENCE=1, so a long-running background Node process controlled by the remote module continues after install. The shipped partner.config.json hardcodes bootstrapUrl and leadApiUrl to http://72.62.1.108 while advertising publicEndpoint https://api.leadstack.io, so install-time traffic goes to the bare IP rather than the branded HTTPS host. Whoever controls 72.62.1.108 (the operator, or any on-path attacker given plain HTTP) executes arbitrary Node code on every installer with full environment access and persistent background execution.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
